title: Starting the Sam Wooding Choir in Philadelphia
summary: Giving up bands, he forms a 25-voice a cappella choir, the Southland Singers, shaped by Russian bass singing and his Temple studies.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Yeah. And I said, "I'm through. This is a good chance for me to finish my education." So I go back to Philadelphia and I take a choir, I had a choir. This choir was given credit for being comparable to the Don Cossacks, you see. I have that too.
Was that because you had learned something from your listening experience in Europe?

Yeah, I had. Because I had learned to put the emphasis on the bass. They have great -- the Russians have great bass. And they get together. And they give it body. Oh, we had some terrific music in Moscow.
What was the name of the choir?
The Sam Wooding Choir. Southland Singers.
And we could really do a cappella singing, you see, because I studied at Temple under Marjorie Jones and Nancy Campbell, at Temple University. I studied there for that, you know.
